question: Should memory-wiki get a plugin-owned per-agent vault scope now, or should this wait for the generic `agents.list[].plugins` override contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent contract affects memory isolation, security posture, config/default surface, CLI/gateway behavior, and upgrade/doctor expectations, so automation should not choose it alone.

options.title: Approve memory-wiki-owned per-agent vault scope
options.body: Add a default-off `memory-wiki` config contract such as `vault.scope: "global" | "per-agent"` with explicit per-agent path resolution, no-context behavior, docs, and two-agent regression proof while leaving generic plugin overrides to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/55401.

options.title: Defer to generic per-agent plugin config
options.body: Keep this issue open as a memory-wiki consumer of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/55401 and implement vault isolation only after the shared plugin config precedence and validation contract exists.

options.title: Reject same-gateway vault isolation for now
options.body: Document separate gateways as the supported hard-isolation boundary and close or narrow memory-wiki vault work to docs and diagnostics only.

recommendation.title: Approve memory-wiki-owned per-agent vault scope
recommendation.body: Add a default-off `memory-wiki` config contract such as `vault.scope: "global" | "per-agent"` with explicit per-agent path resolution, no-context behavior, docs, and two-agent regression proof while leaving generic plugin overrides to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/55401.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans config compatibility, plugin boundaries, and security-sensitive memory isolation, and current history points to steipete as the most relevant product/config decision owner among the likely owners.
